From the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ with $\theta =\frac{x}{3}-1,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1)+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}(2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1)-3+2{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1))\text{d}x & = \\ {\int }_{1}^{2}(2[{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1)+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}-1)]-3)\text{d}x & = \\ {\int }_{1}^{2}(2(1)-3)\text{d}x & = \\ -{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}x & = \\ -x\,{|}_{1}^{2} & = \\ -(2-1) & = \\ -1 & .\end{aligned}
$$
